description: A re-uploaded Blender model is always its latest version; the user's projects keep the meshes they have until asked. This tool asks and answers that one question: choice update_projects without reportId shows which projects and entity templates use an older version (or an earlier import of the same file) and what changed; with the reportId and the projectIds / entityTemplateIds the user chose, it moves just those to the current version. Which ones move is the user's choice; "not now" means no call. Parts are matched by Blender OBJECT name: each takes its new mesh and placement; when only its shape changed it keeps the project's materials and the edits made to them in R3, when its materials changed in Blender it takes Blender's materials, and edits made in R3 to its materials are replaced. Objects new in the model are added under the copy's root Empty, parts the model no longer has are kept (removeGone: true removes them). Published releases never change. Needs the blender:update right.

choice.description: Required: update_projects. There is no default.

entityTemplateIds.description: With a reportId: the entity templates to update.

projectIds.description: With a reportId: the projects to update.

removeGone.description: Also remove the parts the current version no longer has (default false: they are kept and listed). Plan with it and answer that report with it.

reportId.description: The report being answered, from the plan (this tool without reportId). Leave it out to plan.

name: r3_blender_update

answer.description: This answer in words: what was done, what R3 measured, decided or refused, and what to do next. The same text as the result's text block. Read it: the fields beside it are the data, this is the guidance.

title: Update projects to a Blender model's current version
